label: Artemis II Mission Status
delta: Artemis III hardware accelerating: Orion crew+service modules joined Jul 30; all 4 RS-25 engines on site Jul 21; SRB stacking underway; 4 Moon Base landers cleared test milestones Aug 4; Blue Moon MK1 slips to Q1 2027.
deltaNote: Artemis II crew (Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen) completed post-flight reconditioning at JSC. Artemis III crew (Bresnik, Parmitano, Rubio, Douglas) named June 9, now training toward a 2027 Earth-orbit rendezvous/docking test with SpaceX Starship and Blue Origin Blue Moon HLS test articles — NASA selected SpaceX Starlink laser terminals for Orion on July 16 to stream 4K video from the mission. HARDWARE: Orion crew and service modules joined July 30 at KSC's O&C Building, reusing 250+ Artemis II components; combined spacecraft to be powered on next. All four RS-25 core-stage engines delivered from Stennis, on site at KSC by July 21. SLS SRB segments stacking in the VAB since early July, ~4 months ahead of prior schedule; mobile launcher turnaround cut roughly in half. The boosters' aerodynamic nose cones arrived at the VAB Aug 13. MOON BASE: Blue Origin, Firefly, Intuitive Machines and Voyager Technologies each cleared major lander testing milestones by Aug 4, with Voyager's Griffin-1 targeting late-2026 delivery. Starship IFT-13 flew successfully July 24 after the FAA cleared the IFT-12 mishap investigation. ARCHITECTURE: NASA and Northrop Grumman said Aug 6 the cancelled Gateway's HALO module (~$1.9B invested since 2019) will be repurposed into three Lunar Infrastructure Demo missions (LID-1/2/3) feeding Moon Base Phase I; Canada announced the same day it will redirect its Canadarm3 investment from Gateway to Artemis lunar-surface operations. SETBACK: Blue Origin said Aug 6 the May 28 LC-36 explosion traced to a BE-4 main oxygen valve issue; fixed hardware due by end of August, but Blue Moon Mark 1's debut cargo flight — needed for Moon Base I rover delivery — has slipped from late summer 2026 to Q1 2027. NASA and Blue Origin agreed July 24 to New Glenn second-stage hot fire testing at Stennis Space Center starting fall 2026. Aug 14: Administrator Isaacman said he is "extremely confident" Artemis III launches in 2027, detailing a three-launch order — New Glenn/Blue Moon Mk2 first, then SLS/Orion, then Starship V3 — with SpaceX targeting an early-September flight and roughly biweekly launches through year-end.
